$comment: Committed expected failure counts for the Slice-0 thesis invariants.
These numbers are MEASURED, never predicted. Each check exits 0 iff its finding
count equals the number here — a count that DROPS is red too, which forces the
decrement into the same PR as the fix and makes a silent regression impossible
in either direction. A baseline decremented without an accompanying source
change is visible in review as a one-line diff with no fix beside it.
Every entry is currently NON-ZERO on purpose. An invariant that passes on day
one is measuring nothing. When a `blockedBy` slice lands, that slice decrements
its own baseline; when a baseline reaches 0 the `--expect` gate is removed and
the check switches to zero-tolerance (spec Phase 4).

hydration-adoption.reason: FEL-249 / #421 — the fifth invariant, BORN AT ZERO because the two defects it governs (CO5 and DA3) were fixed in the two commits immediately preceding it. This is the documented exception to 'every entry is currently NON-ZERO on purpose'. The rule behind that policy is that a check which CANNOT fail measures nothing; this one demonstrably can, and the demonstration is a committed mutation result rather than an assertion. WHAT IT ADDS OVER check:dual-audience: dual-audience asserts the server EMITS `data-aihu-path` markers; this asserts the client can USE them. Those came apart in production — markers were present and well-formed while addressing a key space the client never queried — and every dual-audience assertion passed on that HTML. SELF-TEST (4 cases, both directions, run before every scan): HA-a carries all three controls — `markerless` renders with `{ hydratable: false }` (the pre-DA3 shape), `disagreeing` renders correct hydratable HTML and then re-keys every marker onto an unreachable sentinel root (the pre-CO5 shape), and `agreeing` re-keys onto whatever root the client currently asks for, proving the checker RECOGNIZES adoption. The controls are keyed to `_ROOT_PATH` rather than to literals, so they test the CHECKER and never production — a self-test whose should-not-flag arm is production reports a real regression as 'the check cannot discriminate' and suppresses the scan that would have named it. HA-b deliberately has NO should-not-flag arm for exactly that reason: any such control would be built from the live router's own bytes. Discrimination is still bidirectional because HA-a exercises the same `assertAdoption` machinery HA-b uses. MEASURED 2026-07-20: 4 self-test cases pass both directions, 2 live probes, 0 findings. MUTATION-VERIFIED: reverting `_ROOT_PATH` (CO5) yields 2 findings while check:dual-audience stays GREEN at 2; dropping `hydratable: true` from packages/router/src/server.ts (DA3) yields 1 finding naming HA-b. Both report the duplicated-content symptom directly ('the primary text appears 2 time(s)') with the self-test still passing.
hydration-adoption.ratchet: Born at 0 and zero-tolerance from day one — there is no ratchet to walk down. Any regression that makes server-rendered HTML unadoptable by the client turns this red: a path-key change on one side of the server/client split, a production `renderToString` call that drops `hydratable: true`, or a hydration walker that rebuilds instead of adopting. The four assertions per probe (innerHTML byte-stability, root node identity, primary text appearing EXACTLY ONCE, and reactive writes reaching the server's own Text node) are four symptoms of one defect and are reported as ONE finding per probe, so the count names distinct entry points — HA-a the direct render, HA-b the live router request — not distinct symptoms.
